speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly where on your leg it hurts, and did you fall or get hurt recently? Also, how long has this limp been going on?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain seem to originate in the hip or groin area, even though he points to the knee? Also, does he experience stiffness or pain first thing in the morning or after resting?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain ever radiate to your hip or groin, and does it feel worse when you twist your leg inward? I need to know if you have any history of similar episodes in the past.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray. REQUEST TEST: Left_Hip_X-Ray. Does the pain get worse when you try to rotate your left leg inward or outward?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Left Hip X-ray findings show flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head consistent with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease. Vital signs are stable: Temperature 36.8°C, Blood Pressure 100/65 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 18 breaths/min. Musculoskeletal examination reveals tenderness on palpation of the left hip, pain elicited with passive motion of the hip, and a full range of motion in the knee. Special tests for the knee (anterior drawer and McMurray's) are negative.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of femoral head flattening and fragmentation confirm the diagnosis of Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease.
